summary: Pass extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 worked through the 26 partly extracted documents of group p5 (Antigua, Brazil, Spain, UK, Greece, EU studies, Ireland, Saint Lucia annual reports, Malta, Nauru, New Zealand, Thailand, Vanuatu). It recorded the figures earlier passes had left for a decision (printed changes, ratios, group shares, other countries' figures in secondary studies, fee and rule restatements, TI annex years as events), the Saint Lucia per-class note movements and variance columns, the Thailand Privilege Card notes and member-profile percentages (OCR, checked against table arithmetic), and labelled what cannot be extracted (charts without values, missing pages, excerpts) with 'Not extractable:'.

observations.notes: TechCabal (14 Feb 2026), as republished in excerpt by Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative. Undated ('once'); no source named for the share. Whether 'government revenue' includes grants is not stated.
observations.location: opening paragraph
observations.quote: In Basseterre, St. Kitts, it once funded 60–70% of government revenue

observations.notes: TechCabal (14 Feb 2026), as republished in excerpt by Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative. Figure attributed to MarketIntelo, a research firm (industry estimate). Bare '$' in a press article: currency left unspecified (decision 5).
observations.location: paragraph 2
observations.quote: The global citizenship-by-investment (CBI) industry, per MarketIntelo, a research firm, was valued at $5.2 billion in 2024

observations.notes: TechCabal (14 Feb 2026), as republished in excerpt by Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative. Projection by unnamed 'analysts' (follows the MarketIntelo valuation). Bare '$': currency unspecified.
observations.location: paragraph 2
observations.quote: with analysts projecting it to hit $12.8 billion by 2033

observations.notes: TechCabal (14 Feb 2026), as republished in excerpt by Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative. Global, all citizenship-by-investment programmes combined; 'at least' stored as a lower bound (value_high empty). Unattributed 'conservative estimates'. Counts people applying, so unit persons.
observations.location: paragraph 2
observations.quote: conservative estimates suggest that globally, at least 10,000 people apply yearly for second citizenships through Investment

observations.notes: TechCabal (14 Feb 2026), as republished in excerpt by Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative. All investment-migration programmes worldwide combined, cumulative 'as of 2022'; 'over' stored as a lower bound. Unattributed. Bare '$': currency unspecified.
observations.location: paragraph 2
observations.quote: with global programmes collectively raising over $20 billion as of 2022

observations.notes: TechCabal (14 Feb 2026), as republished in excerpt by Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative. Egyptian passport (not specific to the programme). The 18 visa-free destinations are already recorded (o-4517c6a82d).
observations.location: Egypt paragraph
observations.quote: Its passport offers 18 visa-free destinations and allows e-visa travel to about 41 other countries globally

observations.notes: TechCabal (14 Feb 2026), as republished in excerpt by Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative. 'fewer than 100' stored as 0 to 100 (DATA_MODEL rule). The same article later gives 98 applications in the first four and a half months (o-8693698fcc).
observations.location: opening paragraph
observations.quote: In São Tomé, fewer than 100 applications in four months have already sparked a new African frontier

Dated to the report year; the underlying transfers are earlier.
events.location: PDF p. 35 (printed p. 33)
events.quote: But instead of transferring €166,831 in application fees to BT International, they sent the money to an offshore company’s (Willerby Trade) account with Pilatus Bank.

new_indicators.name: Market value of the investment-migration industry
new_indicators.definition: Size of the global (or regional) citizenship- or residence-by-investment industry in money terms for a year, as estimated by a research firm or analysts and printed by the source (market research valuations, not money raised by governments). Projections carry status projection.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for TechCabal 2026 (MarketIntelo valuation USD 5.2bn 2024, 12.8bn by 2033). Distinct from cbi_rbi_investment (investment raised through schemes).

new_indicators.name: Destinations reachable with an e-visa
new_indicators.definition: Number of countries passport holders can enter with an electronic visa obtained online before travel (not visa-free and not visa on arrival), as printed. Companion to visa_free_destinations.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for TechCabal 2026 (Egyptian passport: e-visa travel to about 41 other countries).

new_indicators.name: Government revenue excluding CBI, percent of GDP
new_indicators.definition: Total government revenue (tax and non-tax, with or without grants as the source says) excluding citizenship- or residence-by-investment revenue, as a percentage of GDP, as printed. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for IMF Antigua and Barbuda 2025 Article IV, Annex V para 6 (non-CBI total revenue 15.9% of GDP in 2023; ECCU average ex. ATG 24.6%). Companion to fiscal_balance_excl_cbi_pct_gdp.

new_indicators.name: Applications granted as a percentage of applications received
new_indicators.definition: Applications granted in a period (a month or a year) as a percentage of the applications received in a stated period (often the whole fiscal year), as printed by the source; the notes give the base. Not a grant rate on decisions (applications_grant_rate). Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for the Saint Lucia CIU 2017/18 annual report (p. 15 monthly '% of Total Applications Granted' columns, base = the year's applications received). Denied-side figures of the same table use cbi_rejection_rate, as the existing yearly totals do.

new_indicators.name: Programme board members
new_indicators.definition: Members of the board or committee that oversees the programme agency or decides applications, at a date or in a period: a count (unit persons), or, for members with a stated trait (category=, e.g. accredited), the printed percentage (unit percent). Names are never recorded.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for the Saint Lucia CIU 2022/23 annual report (Board of five; sixty percent accredited). Companion to cbi_board_meetings and cbi_board_attendance_share.

new_indicators.name: Change in pending applications (as printed)
new_indicators.definition: Printed change in the number of applications or files pending between two dates, as a count (unit applications) or a percentage (unit percent). Never calculated by us; where both stocks are printed they are recorded separately as applications_pending.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for Movingto (10 Jul 2026) on Greek Golden Visa files, March to May 2026 (-822 / -8.2% investors; -1,796 / -7.0% family; -2,618 / -7.3% total). Companion to applications_received_change_pct.

new_indicators.name: Applications as a percentage of enquiries
new_indicators.definition: Applications received in a period as a percentage of enquiries received (or accepted) in the same period, as printed by the source. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for an IMC industry article on Hong Kong's New CIES (339 applications = 9.1% of 3,700 enquiries, 1 Mar-30 Jun 2024). Companion to enquiries_received.

new_indicators.name: Time taken for an application cap to fill
new_indicators.definition: Time between the opening of an application intake and the moment its cap (quota) was reached, in the unit printed (minutes, hours, days); value_high for 'within N'. Never converted.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for UK MAC (2014) para 4.29: Canada's 700-application federal IIP quota met within 30 minutes of release in 2011.

new_indicators.name: Money committed or allocated from a CBI-financed fund
new_indicators.definition: Money that a fund financed by a citizenship- or residence-by-investment programme (e.g. Malta's NDSF) has committed, pledged or allocated to projects, in total or per project (category=), cumulative to a date, as printed. Not money paid out (cbi_fund_payments).
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for Amphora Media (2025) on Malta's NDSF social projects (EUR 130m allocated to 2022, EUR 131m committed by July 2024, government press-release project list).

new_indicators.name: Share of committed CBI fund money (as printed)
new_indicators.definition: Printed percentage relating money committed to projects from a CBI-financed fund to another amount: the share of commitments already disbursed (category=..._disbursed_of_committed) or commitments as a share of programme revenue (category=..._of_programme_revenue). Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for Amphora Media (2025): social housing 13% disbursed of EUR 60m pledged; less than 10% of the EUR 1.4bn went into social projects.

new_indicators.name: Time from nomination or approval to investment
new_indicators.definition: Average (or other stated measure) time programme applicants take between nominating or being approved for an investment and actually transferring or investing the funds, in the unit printed. Not the authority's processing time (processing_time).
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for MBIE AIP briefings 2024 (average time between nomination and investment of funds about four months).

new_indicators.name: Benefit uses by programme members
new_indicators.definition: Number of times members of a residence programme sold as a membership (e.g. Thailand Privilege/Elite) used or booked a programme benefit (airport assistance, lounges, transfers, spa, government liaison) in a period, in total or by benefit (category=); unit uses for counts, percent for a benefit's printed share of all uses.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for the Thailand Privilege Card annual report FY2568 (214,876 uses; top-5 benefits).

new_indicators.name: Share of a multi-country total
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of a total that spans several countries or programmes (e.g. all approvals in key RBI programmes worldwide, all CBI approvals globally, all investment taken in by EU investment migration programmes) accounted for by one country, programme or group, as printed; category= names the group and the total. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for the EPRS European added value assessment (2021): EU share of global RBI approvals (52% 2015, 36% 2018, 25% 2019) and CBI approvals (9%, 6%), Turkey nearly half of global CBI approvals, PT/ES/EL/LV around 75% of EU RBI, Cyprus about 33% of EU investment intake in 2019.

new_indicators.name: Potential demand for investor programmes
new_indicators.definition: Estimated number of people worldwide (or in a region) who could plausibly use citizenship- or residence-by-investment programmes, as estimated by the source (status estimate).
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for the EPRS EAVA (2021) Annex II: about 4.3 million for RBI and under 400,000 for CBI.

new_indicators.name: Share of a sector's revenue attributed to a CBI programme
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of an economic sector's revenue (e.g. real estate and construction) that the source attributes to a citizenship- or residence-by-investment programme, as printed.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for the EPRS EAVA (2021) main text p. 36 (17% of Cypriot real estate and construction revenue attributed to the CBI), which conflicts with the study's own statements that the sector is 17% of the economy.

new_indicators.name: Average minimum investment across programmes
new_indicators.definition: Average of the minimum investment amounts of several programmes (e.g. the most popular EU schemes), as calculated and printed by the source; the notes list the programmes and amounts used. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for Transparency International / Global Witness 'European Getaway' (2018): average EU entry ticket around EUR 900,000.

new_indicators.name: Programme activity (measure not defined by the source)
new_indicators.definition: Yearly count a source reports as a programme's 'activity' or volume without saying whether it counts applications, approvals, visas or people; kept separate so it is never mixed with defined counts. Unit unspecified.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for the Irish IIP interim evaluation (2018), Table 2.2 (UK Tier 1, US EB-5, Portugal golden visa, Quebec IIP, 2012-2016).

new_indicators.name: Programme figure as a share of a national total
new_indicators.definition: A programme figure expressed by the source as a percentage of a national total of the same kind other than residence permits or naturalisations (which use programme_share_of_grants): e.g. enterprises supported as a share of all active enterprises, programme investment as a share of national FDI. category= names both. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for the Irish IIP interim evaluation (enterprise option supported about 0.02% of active enterprises, 2012-2016).

new_indicators.name: Countries with investor schemes
new_indicators.definition: Number of countries (e.g. EU Member States) offering a citizenship- or residence-by-investment scheme at a date, as counted by the source; category= says which group and scheme type.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for EY's IIP review (2020) relaying the European Commission's January 2019 report: 20 (also given as 18) Member States with RBI schemes and 3 with CBI.

new_indicators.name: Assessment score of a scheme (comparative study)
new_indicators.definition: Score a comparative study assigns to a programme on a stated scale (e.g. the 2018 EPRS scores for access conditions and rights granted, 0-9), as printed; category= names the dimension. Not a count or a money figure.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-partials-p5-2026-10-11 for EY's IIP review (2020): Ireland 5 and 5, UK 4 and 5, European average 5 on the EPRS 2018 scales.
